approach: Write the total length of the one string as the sum of its three segments and use that this length never changes.

steps.text: The string runs from block A, up and over the fixed pulley, down and under the movable pulley, then back up to a fixed point tied off near the fixed pulley. Block B hangs from the movable pulley.
Here yA is how far A hangs below the fixed pulley, yP is how far the movable pulley hangs below the fixed pulley, and y₀ is the fixed tie-off point, so the total length is yA + 2yP minus a constant.
The movable pulley moves with B, so yP is B's position. Differentiate the length equation twice with respect to time; the constant term drops out.
This gives the acceleration relation between A and B, with a minus sign showing they move in opposite vertical directions: when B goes down, A goes up twice as fast, and vice versa.

final_answer.value: aA = 2aB in magnitude, with A and B accelerating in opposite directions (as B moves down, A moves up at twice the rate, and vice versa).

common_mistakes.text: Treating the movable pulley as adding no factor and writing aA = aB, as if it were a simple fixed pulley.
Getting the factor of 2 but putting it on the wrong block, writing aB = 2aA instead of aA = 2aB.
